v.rationale: All three share the same Filament 5 skeleton: Schemas/Tables classes, HasLabel/HasColor enums, #[Scope] scopes, a FilamentUser that returns true from canAccessPanel, and a delete/deleteAny policy. All suites pass (impl-1: 37, impl-2: 36, impl-3: 28 tests). The probes separated them. impl-3 is the only one that keeps resolved_at consistent with status, using an observer. In impl-1 and impl-2, setting a ticket to Resolved through the edit form leaves resolved_at null, so the ticket silently drops out of the required 30-day average. Reopening a ticket also leaves a stale timestamp. impl-3 and impl-1 enforce a unique customer email; impl-2 allows duplicates. All three let non-admins delete a customer, which cascades to that customer's tickets. Bulk delete by non-admins was correctly blocked in every implementation. impl-1 edges out impl-2 on its unique-email rule, its single-query bulk assign, ->authorize('update') on Resolve, and finer-grained tests; it loses points for redundant widget registration and boilerplate policy methods. impl-2 has the most idiomatic minimal policy, but it has the extra duplicate-email bug and a misplaced factory docblock. Ranking: impl-3 > impl-1 > impl-2.
